questions.question: Where is the Wwise SDK 2024.1.18 installed on this machine, and should the Authoring project live in this repo?
questions.answer: Wwise is at `C:\Audiokinetic\Wwise2024.1.18.9194`. The Authoring project goes in this repo. (D-019)

questions.question: Top-level GNU `Makefile` wrapping CMake, or a Windows `build.bat` / `nmake` file?
questions.answer: CMake alone is enough. The original dhewm3 builds with CMake and has no top-level Makefile. A Makefile would only wrap CMake for convenience, so we keep CMake only unless you ask for one.

questions.question: Exact Doom 3 folder under `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\`?
questions.answer: Two options given: classic `...\Steam\steamapps\common\Doom 3`, or `...\DOOM 3 BFG Edition`. Recommendation: classic Doom 3, because dhewm3 runs the original Doom 3 engine data.

questions.question: Should `dhewm3/` stay a submodule, or become a fork of dhewm3?
questions.answer: A submodule is a folder that is its own git repo; our repo only records which commit it is pinned to. Keeping it a submodule keeps upstream pristine, but Phase 1 edits upstream code, so a fork is likely needed. Recommendation: fork before Phase 1.

questions.question: Do students get the original Doom 3 audio files, or only placeholder audio in their Wwise project?
questions.answer: Students get no ID Software audio, only a written list of events and game syncs. We make a template Wwise project ourselves, not shared. Sound choices are ours; using the originals is a good idea. The originals stay on local disk and are never uploaded to GitHub.

questions.question: Windows only for now, or also Linux and macOS?
